title: Diagonal root invariants and the nonnegative exponent lattice
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge1$ an integer invertible in $A$, $\zeta\in A^\times$ satisfy $\zeta^n=1$ and $1-\zeta^a\in A^\times$ for $1\le a<n$, and $r\ge0$. Choose $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$ and a subgroup $H\subseteq(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$. Put
$$B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),\qquad P=\mathbf N^r.$$
Let $H$ fix $A$ and send $x_i$ to $\zeta^{h_i}x_i$. Define
$$L=\{a/n\in(1/n)\mathbf Z^r:\ \textstyle\sum_i h_i a_i=0\pmod n\text{ for all }h\in H\},\qquad Q=L\cap(1/n)\mathbf N^r.$$
Then $Q$ is a fine saturated sharp monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $Q^{\rm gp}=L$, and the inclusion $P\hookrightarrow Q$ is injective with $nQ\subseteq P$. Its group cokernel $L/\mathbf Z^r$ is finite and annihilated by $n$. Here sharp means that the only additive unit is $0$. Give $A$ its $\mathbf Z[P]$-algebra structure by $z^{e_i}\mapsto t_i$, where for any additive monoid $S$, $\mathbf Z[S]$ is free as an abelian group on $z^s$, with $z^sz^{s'}=z^{s+s'}$. There is an $A$-algebra isomorphism
$$A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }B^H,\qquad a\otimes z^q\longmapsto a\prod_i x_i^{nq_i}.$$
It takes $1\otimes z^{e_i}$ to $t_i$. In particular, if $c_q$ denotes the image of $1\otimes z^q$, then $c_q^n=\prod_i t_i^{nq_i}$. This includes $r=0$ and $n=1$ and imposes no regularity or domain assumption on $A$.
